main_text.l: seu Tentoria Nomadum Midianitarum & Æthiopum, pro ipsis Midianitis & Æthiopibus, sumuntur: id quod Iuniores hoc loco obseruare, utile est.

Quartum μεγαλεῖον[?], seu magnificu Dei opus fuit, Æthiopum (qui hoc loco Chusanitæ dicuntur) & Midianitarum, gentium sanè bellicosarum, nominiq; Israe-litarum infensarum, repressionem uoco, tum coercitionem, ne in palantes & sparsos in eremo Israelitas, pro sua libidine, impetum facerent: tum clades, quibus diuersis temporibus affecti sunt, ducibus Pinehas & Gedeone. Numeri 31. & Iudic. 7. & 8.

Posteriores autem uictorias de Midia-nitis partas celebrat Asaphus Propheta, Psalm.83.9 Fac illis sicut Midianitis, sicut Sisaræ, sicut Iabin apud torrentem Kison. Extirpati sunt in Endor: facti sunt stercus terræ. 11. Pone eos, principes eorum, sicut Oreb, & sicut Zeeb: sicut Seba & sicut Salmuna, omnes principes eorum.
Sic autem ratiocinatur Habacucus: Si in gratiam Israelitarum Deus potentissi-mos Reges & bellicosissimas gentes coercuit & repulit, exercitus eorum dele-uit,

page.notes: Doubtful readings: the Greek word "μεγαλεῖον" is marked [?] because the scan is small and the accents are hard to make out. The long s is printed as f throughout (e.g. "fumuntur", "fanè", "Kifon", "ftercus"); I have rendered it as s, as the rules require. "Psalm" appears as "Pfalm" in print, and "Fac illis" is printed with a space. The page ends mid-word ("dele-uit,"), and the sentence continues on the next page. No printing errors were corrected.
